speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing a psychiatric condition alongside a new onset movement disorder. To begin my assessment, have you noticed any specific changes in your mood, thoughts, or behavior recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the background; it is noted that you are a 23-year-old on risperidone with improving psychiatric symptoms. Given the new onset of movement issues, can you describe exactly what involuntary movements you are experiencing, such as stiffness, tremors, or restlessness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. To confirm this and assess the severity, have you noticed any muscle stiffness or tremors in addition to the restlessness? REQUEST TEST: Risperidone serum level.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia (secondary to Risperidone).

The normal risperidone serum levels and the classic description of inner restlessness with fidgeting, pacing, and leg crossing are highly specific for akathisia. We can proceed with management, which typically involves adjusting the dose or adding a beta-blocker like propranolol. Do you have any history of allergic reactions to beta-blockers?
